implementation_notes: On a socket protocol the acknowledgement callback is the return address: the client emits with a callback and the server invokes it (socket.io 4.6+ offers the promise form emitWithAck), while ServerToClientEvents/ClientToServerEvents maps type the response end to end. The address itself is the protocol's ack slot, so the application never serializes one. Use the amqplib variant when the transport is AMQP and the address must be a durable queue name.

variants.name: Socket.IO typed acknowledgement (emitWithAck)
variants.implementation_notes: On a socket protocol the acknowledgement callback is the return address: the client emits with a callback and the server invokes it (socket.io 4.6+ offers the promise form emitWithAck), while ServerToClientEvents/ClientToServerEvents maps type the response end to end. The address itself is the protocol's ack slot, so the application never serializes one. Use the amqplib variant when the transport is AMQP and the address must be a durable queue name.
pitfalls: emitWithAck requires socket.io 4.6+; with older typings the promise form is absent and the timeout option is ignored.
Event maps are compile-time only: a client whose ack payload drifts from the server's type still resolves with the wrong data at runtime.
The ack slot lives only as long as the connection; a server answer produced after disconnect is dropped, so layer an application-level timeout and retry over it.

variants.name: AMQP replyTo property via amqplib (typed publish options)
variants.implementation_notes: In Node services using AMQP, amqplib's typed publish options carry the return address as the broker property: Options.Publish { replyTo, correlationId }, read back from msg.properties and answered with channel.sendToQueue(msg.properties.replyTo, ...). It occupies the same protocol slot as the JavaScript file's realization but is the right variant when the reply destination must survive process restarts (a named reply queue) instead of living in a connection-scoped ack slot.
pitfalls: A named reply queue is shared by every client instance: replies must be matched by correlationId and stale ones expired, or consumers eat each other's messages.
msg.properties.replyTo is attacker-influenced — publishing to it unchecked relays traffic to arbitrary broker destinations.
amqplib's types are structural and cannot catch a correlationId whose type differs between publisher and consumer; share one request-envelope type.
emitWithAck requires socket.io 4.6+; with older typings the promise form is absent and the timeout option is ignored.
Event maps are compile-time only: a client whose ack payload drifts from the server's type still resolves with the wrong data at runtime.
The ack slot lives only as long as the connection; a server answer produced after disconnect is dropped, so layer an application-level timeout and retry over it.
